items.title: Section: Why Nine Kinds of "Complete Understanding" Are Not Faculties At All

items.zh: 問：五根、三十七覺品法，為五攝三十七，三十七攝五耶？答：三十七攝五，非五攝三十七。不攝何等？謂語、業、命、喜、安、捨。如是或六、或四，彼所不攝。問：五根、三根，為五攝三，三攝五耶？答：三攝五，非五攝三。不攝何等？謂意、樂、喜、捨根。問：九遍知幾根攝？答：此九遍知，斷遍知攝故，非根所攝。何等為九？謂欲繫苦集見所斷斷，是初遍知。色無色繫苦集見所斷斷，第二遍知。欲繫滅見所斷斷，第三遍知。色無色繫滅見所斷斷，第四遍知。欲繫道見所斷斷，第五遍知。色無色繫道見所斷斷，第六遍知。
items.en: Question: do the five faculties subsume the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, or the reverse? Answer: the thirty-seven subsume the five, not the reverse. Question: do the five faculties subsume the three faculties of realisation, or the reverse? Answer: the three subsume the five, not the reverse. Question: how many of the twenty-two faculties subsume the nine kinds of complete understanding? Answer: none, since complete understanding is subsumed under severing through understanding, not under any faculty. What are the nine? What the path of vision severs concerning the desire realm's truths of suffering and origin is the first. The same for the form and formless realms is the second. What it severs concerning the desire realm's truth of cessation is the third. The same for the form and formless realms is the fourth. The desire realm's truth of the path is the fifth. The form and formless realms' truth of the path is the sixth.

items.title: Section: Completing the Nine Understandings, and Opening the Buddha's Own Unique Qualities

items.zh: 下分結斷，第七遍知。色愛盡，第八遍知。無色愛盡，第九遍知。當知遍知略由二緣而得建立。一、通達諦斷故；二、永度界斷故。由相同分、界不同分及同分故，立二遍知。相不同分、界不同分及同分故，立四遍知。永度劣界故，立一遍知。永度中界故，立一遍知。永度妙界故，立一遍知。問：諸相、隨好、力、無畏等不共佛法，幾根攝耶？
items.en: The severing of the lower fetters is the seventh complete understanding. The exhaustion of craving for form is the eighth. The exhaustion of craving for the formless is the ninth. It should be understood that complete understanding is, in brief, established through two conditions: comprehending the truths, and permanently transcending each realm. Question: how many of the twenty-two faculties subsume the excellent marks, minor marks, powers, fearlessness, and other qualities unique to a buddha?

items.title: Section: Which Faculties Ground a Buddha's Excellent Marks — Including Why Everything Tastes Like Nectar

items.zh: 答：諸相、隨好，舌根及四根依處所攝。
items.en: Answer: the excellent marks and minor marks are subsumed under the tongue faculty, together with the physical basis of four faculties.

items.zh: 何等為四？謂身根、男根、眼根、舌根。

items.title: Section: The Empty Perfume Bottle — Why Only a Buddha Truly Severs Every Trace

items.zh: 諸佛十力，如來身中慧根所攝，及具知根。四無所畏，五根所攝，及即此一。如無所畏，不護亦爾。三種念住，非根所攝，然六根所引無貪、無瞋所攝。大悲，亦彼所引無瞋、無癡所攝，非根所攝。無忘失法，如力應知。佛一切種妙智亦爾。永斷習氣，非根所攝，然是六根所證煩惱永斷所攝。問：諸煩惱品所有麁重，阿羅漢等永斷無餘；復有何品麁重，阿羅漢等所未能斷，由斷此故，說名如來永斷習氣？答：異熟品麁重，阿羅漢等所未能斷，唯有如來名究竟斷。
items.en: The ten powers of the Buddha are subsumed under the wisdom faculty within the Tathāgata's own being, together with the faculty of complete knowledge. The four kinds of fearlessness are subsumed under the five faculties, together with that same faculty. The three foundations of mindfulness are not subsumed under any faculty, but under the freedom from greed and hatred generated by six faculties. Great compassion is likewise subsumed under the freedom from hatred and delusion those same faculties generate, not under any faculty itself. The permanent severing of habitual tendencies is not subsumed under any faculty, but under the permanent severing of affliction those six faculties bring about. Question: every affliction's own coarse habitual residue has already been permanently severed without remainder by arhats and the like — what further residue remains unsevered by them, such that severing it alone earns the name of the Tathāgata's own permanent severing of habitual tendencies? Answer: the coarse residue bound up with karmic ripening itself, which arhats and the like have not yet severed — only the Tathāgata is said to sever it to completion.

items.title: Section: Four Kinds of Food That Nourish the Body and Mind Alike

items.zh: 問：如經言：有四種食，皆能長養諸根大種。云何四食？云何長養諸根大種？答：段食、觸食、意思食、識食。由此四種，長養五色根及意根，并根所依所有大種。
items.en: Question: as the sūtra says, there are four kinds of food, all capable of nourishing the faculties and their great elements. What are the four, and how do they nourish? Answer: solid food, the food of contact, the food of mental volition, and the food of consciousness. Through these four, the five physical faculties and the mind faculty are nourished, together with all the great elements those faculties depend upon.

items.title: Section: Why Sleep Doesn't Count as Food, Even Though It Also Sustains the Body

items.zh: 問：云何段食？答：諸所食噉，若能長養諸根大種；與此相違，當知非食。如段食，餘食、非食，應知亦爾。問：段食云何能作食事？乃至識食亦爾。答：若諸段食，能攝益識令其強盛；由此長養諸根大種，亦令強盛。觸能攝受若喜、若樂、若捨一分，由此復能攝益諸識；由攝益故，復能長養諸根大種。意思為欲證得可愛境界相故，依正方便，起染不染希望喜根，緣未來境攝益於識，由此長養諸根大種。如是三食攝益其識，由體增盛及緣現在、未來生故，識復長養諸根大種。故立四食。問云：何識與意根為食？答：由三資持所任持故，能與後後為增盛因，令彼得生。問：何故眠夢、梵行、等至皆能長養諸根大種，而不立食？答：有二種長養。一、攝受別義長養，二、令無損害長養。眠夢等法，於後長養雖能長養，於前即非，是故不立。問：何故命根能任持身，而不立食？答：若離於食，彼終不能長養身故。
items.en: Question: what is solid food? Answer: whatever is eaten and thereby nourishes the faculties and great elements; the opposite is not food. Question: why do sleep, celibate discipline, and meditative attainment, though all capable of nourishing the faculties and elements, not count as food? Answer: there are two kinds of nourishment — special, positive nourishment, and simple freedom from harm. Sleep and the rest provide the latter but not the former, and so are not classified as food. Question: why does the life faculty, which sustains the body, not count as food? Answer: because without food, it could never actually nourish the body at all.

items.title: Section: Why Heaven Has No Need for Toilets

items.zh: 問：何等段食名麁？答：若非天所食。問：何等名細？答：諸天所食。由彼食已，即於身中便自消化，非漸次故。
items.en: Question: what solid food is called coarse? Answer: whatever the gods do not eat. Question: what is called subtle? Answer: what the gods eat, since once eaten it is immediately digested within the body itself, not gradually.

blocks.text: From the faculties to a buddha's qualities, and then the four kinds of food.
These nine belong to understanding as severing, not to any faculty. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first six are the path of seeing's severing, by realm and by truth.
Master Cháng Bǎi names the tongue, body, male, and eye faculties, with their supporting matter.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the ten powers include the five wholesome faculties, not wisdom alone. Arhats and solitary realisers leave behind the coarse residue of affliction, but not the residue bound with the ripened body; only a buddha removes every trace. (Ru-Yi's heading compares this to an empty perfume bottle that still smells.)
Solid food, contact, volition, and consciousness. Master Cháng Bǎi: they nourish the faculties and mind, with the elements that support them.
Food must positively nourish; sleep, celibacy, and attainment only keep away harm.
The empty perfume bottle: the arhat's afflictions are gone, yet a scent of habit remains. Only in a buddha is nothing left at all.

quiz.q: How do the first six of the nine understandings differ from the last three?
options: the first six are cultivation's; the last three are vision's, completed first
the first six are vision's severing by realm and truth; the last three are the lower fetters, craving for form, and for the formless
all nine are vision's
all nine are cultivation's
quiz.why: The first six are the path of vision's severing by realm and truth. Master Cháng Bǎi: at the path of vision, severing the conceptual afflictions of the desire realm's truths of suffering and origin is the first understanding; at the path of cultivation, exhausting desire-realm craving is the seventh. The treatise: comprehending truths and transcending realms.

quiz.q: Why are the nine understandings not subsumed under the twenty-two?
options: understanding is wisdom and so lies within the wisdom faculty, "not subsumed" being a manner of speaking
because understanding is an outsiders' teaching
because it belongs only to the Buddha
understanding is explained by what is severed, being of the severing type, and so lies outside the faculties
quiz.why: The treatise says these nine belong to understanding as severing, not to any faculty. Master Cháng Bǎi: understanding is explained here by the afflictions severed, and so it is outside the twenty-two. Severing at vision is called comprehending the truths. The English is clear on this point.

quiz.q: Under what are the marks and minor marks subsumed?
options: the body faculty alone, marks being on the body, other faculties being unrelated
mind with faith and the rest
no faculty
the tongue faculty and the physical basis of four faculties
quiz.why: The treatise gives the tongue faculty and the basis of four faculties. Master Cháng Bǎi: the tongue, body, male, and eye faculties, with the sense-supporting matter on which these rest. He notes that, the mind being free of greed, hatred, and delusion, anything in the Buddha's mouth becomes the finest taste.

quiz.q: The ten powers are under wisdom. What does Master Cháng Bǎi add?
options: the powers are wisdom alone, the Buddha having gone beyond faith
the powers are physical strength
the powers include faith and the rest; wisdom being chief in illuminating objects, it is named
the powers lie under life
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the ten powers are not only wisdom; they also include the five wholesome faculties, faith and the rest. Since wisdom's function of illuminating objects is outstanding, the treatise names wisdom by the chief element. The English "within the Tathāgata's own being" renders 身中 well.

quiz.q: What coarse residue is left by arhats and severed only by the Tathāgata, and what image does the lecture use?
options: the coarse residue of affliction, shown by smoke remaining after a lamp goes out, which means arhats still retain affliction seeds and have not truly severed affliction
the coarse residue of ripening; fragrance lingering for arhats, gone even of scent for the Buddha
the cognitive obstruction; a mirror
the body; a boat
quiz.why: The treatise distinguishes the coarse residue of affliction, gone in arhats, from that bound with ripening. Master Cháng Bǎi: the coarse residue of the ripened body is left by arhats and solitary realisers; lingering fragrance is the arhat's unsevered habit, and no fragrance at all the Buddha's severing.

quiz.q: What are the four foods and what do they nourish?
options: solid food, contact, volition, consciousness; nourishing the five physical faculties, mind, and their elements
solid food, meditative delight, Dharma joy, vows; nourishing faith and the three
form, sound, smell, taste; nourishing life
sleep, dream, celibacy, attainment; nourishing the body
quiz.why: The treatise names solid food, contact, volition, and consciousness. Master Cháng Bǎi: these nourish the five clear physical faculties and mind, along with the four elements of the supporting matter on which those faculties rest; desire-realm beings need all four to live.

quiz.q: Why are sleep, celibacy, and attainment not food, and why not the life faculty?
options: they are positive nourishment, finer than food; life is itself food, needing no separate listing
they nourish by freedom from harm, not by positive nourishment; life without food cannot nourish the body
because they are evil
because they do not nourish at all
quiz.why: The treatise distinguishes positive nourishment from freedom from harm. Master Cháng Bǎi: sleep, celibacy, and attainment belong to freedom from harm; food proper must be able to nourish faculties and elements. The life faculty, without food, could not nourish the body. The English rendering is clear here.
